summary: Teach accelerator comparison as a method using individually sourced current or historical case studies.
outcomes: Compare dataflow, memory, software support and deployment constraints.
Separate historical architectures from currently supported purchase/deployment options.
sequence: Define a fixed workload and evaluation criteria.
Draw one documented dataflow per selected accelerator.
Map precision, memory and compilation constraints.
Check current SDK, hardware and lifecycle status.
Compare evidence and identify where no fair benchmark exists.

visual.question: Which architectural or software constraint prevents a like-for-like run?
visual.interaction: Inspect capability and evidence cells rather than rank by a single peak metric.

practice.task: Write two sourced case studies with explicit lifecycle and evidence dates.
practice.success: Claims distinguish official capabilities, measured outcomes and unavailable information.
